h: The Great Shofar and Secrets That Enter the Heart

p: and may we behold His glory…" and so on.
In the commentary on the zemiros
by Rabbi Yisrael Saruk, of blessed memory,
he wrote: "shofreih — His shofar…" and so on.
וְהוּא הָיָה מִגּוּרֵי הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
And he was among the disciples of the Arizal,
that the great shofar is Binah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רסו, ב)
as is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 266b);
and the second meal of Shabbos
is called in the holy Zohar
וּבְרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צב, א)
and in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Zohar II 92a)
For at this meal, which is that of Atika,
we ask, "May He send us His shofar":
that is, the great shofar, which is Binah.
That is, at the meal of Shabbos night
שֶׁהוּא סְעוּדָתוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for it is the meal of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him
as we say in the blessing Magen Avos:
"Before Him we serve with fear and dread."
And through fear one comes to teshuvah,
"'Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem':
fortunate is he who does teshuvah
"The goal of wisdom is teshuvah…" and so on,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת ה׳ וְגוֹ׳
"as it says, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem…'"
"Then you will understand the fear of Hashem";
and then one merits the supernal teshuvah.
And this is why we say at the second meal,
which is the great shofar, Binah.
And this is what is said in the commentary mentioned above:
the shofar that Melech HaMashiach will blow.
in which "and He said" is not stated,
for it is hidden from all thought,
וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם
"And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters";
"This is the spirit of Melech HaMashiach.
which is likened to water…" and so on.
for whose sake the whole world is forgiven,
And certainly there will not avail
the teshuvah of an individual for the whole world
that he will bring a thought of teshuvah,
into the heart of the whole world.
for David is "the man who was raised up on high"
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah
"And David My servant shall be their prince forever";
And he will be the individual who repented,
and for his sake the whole world will be forgiven.
And this is the great shofar
And it is hinted in the utterance "Bereishis,"
which corresponds to Keser Elyon, Atika;
and it is written of him (Daniel 7:13):
"And behold, with the clouds of heaven
one like a son of man came,
and he reached the Ancient of Days,
and they brought him near before Him…"
Therefore we ask at the meal of Atika,
then you will understand the fear of Hashem,
and you will find knowledge of God."
That is, from the joining of Chochmah and Binah,
knowledge of God comes into the heart.
And this is why we say, "and may we behold":
of itself, by way of a find,
that is, the holiness of Atika;
"And his eye saw every precious thing";
and they said in the Midrash
"This is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues;
things that were not revealed to Moshe
were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues."
And this is the fiftieth gate
of the fifty gates of Binah,
and it belongs to the baal teshuvah,
and it is the inwardness of Keser Elyon,
such that he said of himself,
"When I was an am ha'aretz…" and so on,
to him the fiftieth gate was revealed;
and it is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
That is not so for Moshe Rabbeinu,
for when he was born the house filled with light,
so that he knew no evil at all;
"And may He show us His secret":
that was hidden away for the tzaddikim,
that You have hidden away for those who fear You."
"And may He show us…" and so on,
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ג, ד)
This is according to what they said (Bereishis Rabbah 3:4):
מְלַמֵּד שֶׁנִּתְעַטֵּף בָּהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
This teaches that HaKadosh Baruch Hu wrapped Himself in it
and the radiance of His splendor shone…" and so on;
"he told it to him in a whisper.
He said to him: It is an explicit pasuk:
'He wraps Himself in light as a garment'
and you told it to me in a whisper?!
Just as I received it in a whisper,
so I told it to you in a whisper."
how this is an answer to his question
because he received it in a whisper.
But the matter of a whisper
הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
is in the manner of what they said in the holy Zohar
וּכְעֵין מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רלד, ב)
and similar to what is written (Zohar I 234b):
as it is said, 'and you say in your heart'
that one should feel it in the depth of the heart.
That is, by saying to him,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה הִכְנִיס בּוֹ הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב
thereby he instilled in him a feeling in the heart
And this is what he said,
"Just as I received it in a whisper":
that is, it shone into his heart
to feel the light, "that it was good";
"so I told it to you in a whisper,"
even though it is an explicit pasuk,
he too would feel the light in the heart.
And as we have said several times
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing
for the life of the World to Come,
that even in the Written Torah
of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
and made it known…" and so on.
only the pasuk as it stands,
had been corrupt in this matter,
even though he heard from him
And we have said a proof
from what Rebbi taught in the Mishnah
felt in it a renewed light
from the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh.
which is told in a whisper."
